correctness.rationale: For every k>=1, the normalized quadratic Gauss sum at a nonzero frequency difference is zero precisely when after removing their common 2-power either m=1 and U+V odd or m>=2 and U odd. At m>=2 an odd U cancels by half-period translation; if U even and V odd the two surviving terms in the squared modulus give 2^(m+1)>0. The lowest-differing-bit orthogonality rule forces two occupied child prefixes per occupied node; a full N=2^k family uniquely yields a 1-Lipschitz f on residues mod 2^(k−1) and one of four terminal H/V edges per residue. The count of f is 2^(2^k−2), times 4^(2^(k−1)) terminal choices, hence 2^(2^(k+1)−2). End k=1 is four edges. Exact checks of all Gauss sums for k=1..5 and constructed spectra k<=3 corroborate, not prove, the all-k statement.
